questions.q: Per this lesson, why does Priya treat documentation as a required deliverable rather than a nice-to-have?
options: Because the real test of a platform build is whether a second developer could pick it up without the original builder in the room
Because Salesforce requires documentation to allow code to compile
Because documentation replaces the need for test coverage
Because the Definition of Done does not actually mention documentation
questions.explain: The lesson states documentation is explicitly listed in the Definition of Done because a build only you understand isn't really finished -- someone else needs to be able to maintain it.

questions.q: What five sections make up this lesson's required ADR format?
options: Title, Author, Date, Signature, Approval
Summary, Risks, Budget, Timeline, Owner
Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences
Problem, Solution, Code, Tests, Deployment
questions.explain: The ADR format shown is Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, and Consequences.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the "Alternatives considered" section matters as much as the Decision section itself?
options: It's just a formality with no real value
It is the only section Salesforce reviews validate
It must list at least ten alternatives to be valid
It's the part that actually proves the decision was reasoned rather than accidental, and the part most documentation skips
questions.explain: The lesson calls out Alternatives considered as the section that proves the decision was deliberate -- and notes it's the part most real-world documentation tends to skip.

questions.q: What is the difference between the entity-relationship diagram (ERD) from Lesson 3 and the data dictionary built in this lesson?
options: They are the same document with two different names
The ERD shows how objects connect; the data dictionary describes, field by field, what each custom field means in plain language
The data dictionary replaces the need for an ERD entirely
The ERD is for developers only; the data dictionary is only for Apex classes, not fields
questions.explain: The ERD answers 'what connects to what'; the data dictionary answers 'what does this specific field mean and why does it exist' -- two distinct, complementary documents.

questions.q: How many ADRs does this capstone require, per this lesson, and what is one of the specific decisions covered?
options: Exactly one ADR, covering only the data model
Zero ADRs; documentation here means only the data dictionary
At least five ADRs, including the Flow-vs-Apex decision from Lesson 2 and the Queueable-vs-future decision
Twenty-five ADRs, one per lesson
questions.explain: The lesson requires at least five ADRs, specifically naming the Flow-vs-Apex call, the Queueable-vs-future call, the lookup-vs-master-detail call, the OWD choices, and the Named Credential/exception design.
